name: 82. Flattened namespace tool names honour each wire tool-name limit (namespace-alias-length)
description: Companion to folder 79 (#7048). Flattening a Responses `namespace` tool renames each nested function to `<namespace>__<function>`. Each wire caps tool names by its own documented contract: OpenAI-compatible wires, Bedrock Converse and Fireworks at 64 characters of [A-Za-z0-9_-]; Anthropic at 128; Gemini and Vertex at 128 with '.' and ':' also allowed; providers that document no limit take the OpenAI-compatible 64. The pre-fix alias had no cap, so a Codex MCP namespace plus a tool name could exceed the wire limit and the provider answered 400 on a name the caller never sent. The alias is now capped per base provider (datasheet row tool_name_max_length overrides), deterministically: plain when it fits, otherwise an 8-hex hash prefix plus the function name. Both rows send the same 64-char namespace with two functions (a 98-char plain alias) and pin the outbound names through raw_request: on Anthropic the alias stays plain under 128; on DeepSeek, an Anthropic-wire provider with no documented limit, it takes the hashed form under 64. Run: make run-provider-harness-test PROVIDER=<anthropic|deepseek> FEATURE="namespace-alias-length" PARALLEL=0

item.name: anthropic/claude-haiku-4-5 /v1/responses 64-char namespace with two functions: 98-char alias stays plain under the 128-char Anthropic limit (raw_request) - namespace-alias-length

exec: // 400 is deliberately NOT skipped: an over-length or malformed tool name is the failure signature.
pm.test('anthropic haiku-4-5, 128-char wire: request accepted - namespace-alias-length', function () {
var text = pm.response.text() || '';
pm.expect(pm.response.code, 'request failed: ' + text.slice(0, 600)).to.be.below(400);
if (pm.response.code >= 400) { return; }
var body = pm.response.json() || {};
var ef = body.extra_fields || {};
var rr = ef.raw_request;
if (typeof rr === 'string') { try { rr = JSON.parse(rr); } catch (e) { rr = null; } }
pm.test('anthropic haiku-4-5, 128-char wire: raw_request captured', function () {
pm.expect(rr, 'raw_request missing - x-bf-send-back-raw-request not honored').to.be.an('object');
if (!rr || typeof rr !== 'object') { return; }
var tools = rr.tools || [];
pm.test('anthropic haiku-4-5, 128-char wire: both nested functions reach the wire as distinct tools', function () {
pm.expect(tools.length, 'expected two outbound tools: ' + JSON.stringify(rr).slice(0, 400)).to.equal(2);
pm.expect(tools[0].name, 'the two flattened names must stay distinct').to.not.equal(tools[1].name);
pm.test('anthropic haiku-4-5: names honour the 128-char Anthropic contract and stay plain - namespace-alias-length', function () {
for (var i = 0; i < tools.length; i++) {
var name = tools[i].name || '';
pm.expect(name, 'tool[' + i + '] name ' + JSON.stringify(name) + ' (len ' + name.length + ') breaks the 128-char Anthropic contract').to.match(/^[A-Za-z0-9_-]{1,128}$/);

pm.expect(tools[0].name, 'a 98-char alias fits the Anthropic limit and must not be hashed').to.equal("mcp__server_with_a_very_long_name_server_with_a_very_long_name_x__read_repository_file_contents_v2");

item.name: bedrock/us.moonshotai.kimi-k3 /v1/responses over-64-char namespace alias: hashed name is letter-first so kimi answers (was digit-leading, empty stream) (raw_request) - namespace-alias-length

exec: // Bifrost hashes an over-64-char namespace alias to <hash>_<function>. A bare 8-hex
// hash starts with a digit 10 times in 16, and moonshotai.kimi-k3 on Bedrock answers
// any digit-leading tool name with HTTP 200 and an empty stream (Codex: 0 tokens, no
// text). This namespace hashes to 7e4a44cb under the old scheme, so pre-fix the wire
// carries '7e4a44cb_execute_document_command' and the model never answers.
var txt = pm.response.text() || '';
var body = {};
try { body = pm.response.json() || {}; } catch (e) { body = {}; }
var rr = (body.extra_fields || {}).raw_request;
if (typeof rr === 'string') { try { rr = JSON.parse(rr); } catch (e) { rr = null; } }
var tools = ((rr || {}).toolConfig || {}).tools || [];
var names = tools.map(function (t) { return (t.toolSpec || {}).name || ''; });
pm.test('bedrock kimi-k3: request accepted - namespace-alias-length', function () {
pm.expect(pm.response.code, 'want 200: ' + txt.slice(0, 600)).to.eql(200);
pm.expect(rr, 'raw_request missing or unparseable: ' + txt.slice(0, 300)).to.be.an('object');
pm.test('bedrock kimi-k3: hashed alias is letter-first on the wire - namespace-alias-length', function () {
pm.expect(names, 'outbound tool names: ' + JSON.stringify(names)).to.eql(['t7e4a44cb_execute_document_command']);
pm.expect(names[0], 'a digit-leading tool name makes kimi-k3 return an empty stream').to.match(/^[A-Za-z]/);
pm.test('bedrock kimi-k3: the model answers - namespace-alias-length', function () {
// Positive usage alone is not an answer. The model must either reply in text or
// call the tool, and a call must come back under the caller's own namespace and
// name: the hashed alias is Bifrost's wire name and must never leak to the client.
var NS = 'mcp__codex_apps__codex_document_control_harness_alias_00';
var output = body.output || [];
var text = output.filter(function (o) { return o && o.type === 'message'; }).map(function (o) {
return (o.content || []).filter(function (c) { return c && c.type === 'output_text'; }).map(function (c) { return c.text || ''; }).join('');
var calls = output.filter(function (o) { return o && o.type === 'function_call'; });
var restored = calls.filter(function (o) { return o.name === 'execute_document_command' && o.namespace === NS; });

pm.expect(text.trim().length > 0 || restored.length > 0, 'want output_text or a function_call restored to ' + NS + '/execute_document_command, got output: ' + JSON.stringify(output).slice(0, 400) + ' body: ' + txt.slice(0, 300)).to.be.true;
pm.expect(calls.length, 'every function_call must be restored to the caller namespace and name: ' + JSON.stringify(calls).slice(0, 300)).to.equal(restored.length);
